TST-0088.evidence_requirement: the truncated artifact preserved as a fixture with its byte length, plus the classification and the condition id that rejected it

TST-0090.evidence_requirement: a run in which the original dispatcher is frozen past lease expiry, the unit is reclaimed and completed, and the thawed original's write is then REJECTED with its stale token recorded
TST-0090.question_or_target: Phase 9 requires work claims, file leases, conflict detection and duplicate-work suppression (:10972-10975). Target: when the dispatcher holding a unit's lease dies, a new dispatcher may reclaim the unit after lease expiry, and the ORIGINAL must be unable to commit a late result afterwards - a monotonically increasing fencing token, not a timeout alone, is what makes reclaim safe. Question: can a zombie dispatcher that wakes after expiry still write a receipt? (Monitor-death observation is TST-0089; mtime-based stall detection is owned by TST-0152 in slice TST-2.)

TST-0090.reviewer_requirement: one fresh-context adversarial reviewer from the OTHER vendor than the author (Claude author -> Codex reviewer, and the reverse); a same-vendor reviewer inherits the author's blind spots
TST-0090.title: Orphaned work must be reclaimable exactly once: lease expiry with a fencing token

TST-0091.evidence_requirement: a batch of N units with one deliberately hung: the barrier must resolve within the declared timeout with N-1 results plus one typed timeout classification
TST-0091.question_or_target: Failure class :11317. Measured: parallel() has no per-agent timeout, so one hung agent deadlocks the whole phase - detected only by a write-freeze longer than 25 minutes. Target: per-unit timeouts and a per-work-unit pipeline so the barrier resolves on the survivors with the hung unit classified, not silently awaited.

TST-0092.evidence_requirement: sliding-window arrival counts computed from a simulated dispatch of >=1000 units at several caps, with the max observed window rate printed per cap | substrate note: runs cloud-batch because pure scheduler simulation over >=1000 generated schedules; no local state touched
TST-0092.question_or_target: Spec: 'Stagger arrivals to avoid 429 thundering-herd failures. Treat quota and arrival rate as scheduler inputs' (:10577-10578). Target: a property test over the scheduler asserting that for any batch size and any declared rate cap, the realised inter-arrival distribution never exceeds the cap in any sliding window. Distinct from TST-0093, which tests the RESPONSE to a 429 rather than its prevention.
TST-0092.retry_policy: unlimited re-runs ONLY with a new recorded seed; re-running the same seed is not a retry, it is a reproduction and must produce the identical verdict
TST-0092.reviewer_requirement: one cross-vendor refuter plus one statistics reviewer who re-derives the variance band from the raw per-run numbers, not from the summary

TST-0092.title: Arrival-rate scheduler: stagger and jitter as a measured property

TST-0100.evidence_requirement: the guard demonstrated refusing a write in a scratch clone of a DIFFERENT repository, and permitting it in the pinned one
